arxiv-2206-03949.title: Nonlocal traffic models with general kernels: singular limit, entropy admissibility, and convergence rate
arxiv-2206-03949.creator: Maria Colombo, Gianluca Crippa, Elio Marconi, Laura V. Spinolo
arxiv-2206-03949.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Maria Colombo, Gianluca Crippa, Elio Marconi, Laura V. Spinolo. Nonlocal conservation laws (the signature feature being that the flux function depends on the solution through the convolution with a given kernel) are extensively used in the modeling of vehicular traffic. In this work we discuss the singular local limit, namely the convergence of the nonlocal solutions to the entropy admissible solution of the conservation
law obtained by replacing the convolution kernel with a Dirac delta.

arxiv-2211-01482.title: RQUGE: Reference-Free Metric for Evaluating Question Generation by Answering the Question
arxiv-2211-01482.creator: Alireza Mohammadshahi Thomas Scialom Majid Yazdani, Pouya Yanki Angela Fan James Henderson Marzieh Saeidi
arxiv-2211-01482.description: Abstract Existing metrics for evaluating the quality of automatically generated questions such as BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and BLEURT compare the reference and predicted questions, providing a high score when there is a considerable lexical overlap or semantic similarity between the candidate and the reference questions. This approach has two major shortcomings. First, we need expensive human-provided reference questions.

We study the distribution of the sequences p n ( mod m ) p_{n}\pmod{m} and q n ( mod m ) q_{n}\pmod{m} with a fixed modulus m m , and more generally, the distribution of the 2 × 2 2\times 2 matrix with entries p n − 1 , p n , q n − 1 , q n ( mod m ) p_{n-1},p_{n},q_{n-1},q_{n}\pmod{m} .

arxiv-2304-11299.creator: Yuanyuan Li School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, 230026, China E-mails: lyuanyuan@mail.ustc.edu.cn
arxiv-2304-11299.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuanyuan Li School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, 230026, China E-mails: lyuanyuan@mail.ustc.edu.cn. In this paper, we solve the L p L_{p} chord Minkowski problem in the case of discrete measures whose supports are in general position for negative p p and q > 0 . As for general Borel measure with a density, we also give a proof but need p ∈ ( − n , 0 ) p\in(-n,0) and n + 1 > q ⩾ 1 .

arxiv-2305-14194.title: A Spatial Interference Approach to Account for Mobility in Air Pollution Studies with Multivariate Continuous Treatments
arxiv-2305-14194.creator: Heejun Shin, Danielle Braun, Kezia Irene, Michelle Audirac, Joseph Antonelli
arxiv-2305-14194.description: Abstract We develop new methodology to improve our understanding of the causal effects of multivariate air pollution exposures on public health. Typically, exposure to air pollution for an individual is measured at their home geographic region, though people travel to different regions with potentially different levels of air pollution.

arxiv-2310-14952.title: 8+8=4: Formalizing Time Units to Handle Symbolic Music Durations
arxiv-2310-14952.creator: Emmanouil Karystinaios, Francesco Foscarin, Florent Jacquemard, Masahiko Sakai, Satoshi Tojo, Gerhard Widmer
arxiv-2310-14952.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Emmanouil Karystinaios, Francesco Foscarin, Florent Jacquemard, Masahiko Sakai, Satoshi Tojo, Gerhard Widmer. This paper focuses on the nominal durations of musical events (notes and rests) in a symbolic musical score, and on how to conveniently handle these in computer applications. We propose the usage of a temporal unit that is directly related to the graphical symbols in musical scores, and pair this with a set of operations that cover typical computations in music applications.

arxiv-2312-02351.title: No U(1) ‘electric-magnetic’ duality in Einstein gravity
arxiv-2312-02351.creator: Ricardo Monteiro
arxiv-2312-02351.description: Abstract We revisit the question of whether classical general relativity obeys, beyond the linearised order, an analogue of the global U(1) electric-magnetic duality of Maxwell theory, with the Riemann tensor playing the role analogous to the field strength. Following contradictory claims in the literature, we present a simple gauge-invariant argument that the duality does not hold.

arxiv-2404-04496.title: Towards Better Graph Neural Network-based Fault Localization Through Enhanced Code Representation
arxiv-2404-04496.creator: Md Nakhla Rafi, Dong Jae Kim, An Ran Chen, Tse-Hsun (Peter) Chen, Shaowei Wang
arxiv-2404-04496.description: Abstract . Automatic software fault localization plays an important role in software quality assurance by pinpointing faulty locations for easier debugging. Coverage-based fault localization is a commonly used technique, which applies statistics on coverage spectra to rank faulty code based on suspiciousness scores. However, statistics-based approaches based on formulae are often rigid, which calls for learning-based techniques.

arxiv-2411-19650.title: CogACT : A Foundational Vision-Language-Action Model for Synergizing Cognition and Action in Robotic Manipulation
arxiv-2411-19650.creator: Qixiu Li ​ Yaobo Liang Zeyu Wang Lin Luo Xi Chen Mozheng Liao Fangyun Wei, Yu Deng Sicheng Xu Yizhong Zhang Xiaofan Wang Bei Liu Jianlong Fu Jianmin Bao, Dong Chen Yuanchun Shi Jiaolong Yang Baining Guo
arxiv-2411-19650.description: Abstract The advancement of large Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models has significantly improved robotic manipulation in terms of language-guided task execution and generalization to unseen scenarios. While existing VLAs adapted from pretrained large Vision-Language-Models (VLM) have demonstrated promising generalizability, their task performance is still unsatisfactory as indicated by the low tasks success rates in different environments.

arxiv-2504-13314.creator: Timothy Tjhay, Ricardo J. Bessa, José Paulos
arxiv-2504-13314.description: Abstract The European Union’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act defines robustness, resilience, and security requirements for high-risk sectors but lacks detailed methodologies for assessment. This paper introduces a novel framework for quantitatively evaluating the robustness and resilience of reinforcement learning agents in congestion management.

arxiv-2505-16734.title: Maximum Total Correlation Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2505-16734.creator: Bang You, Puze Liu, Huaping Liu, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz
arxiv-2505-16734.description: Abstract Simplicity is a powerful inductive bias. In reinforcement learning, regularization is used for simpler policies, data augmentation for simpler representations, and sparse reward functions for simpler objectives, all that, with the underlying motivation to increase generalizability and robustness by focusing on the essentials. Supplementary to these techniques, we investigate how to promote simple behavior throughout the episode.

arxiv-2602-02645.title: Complexity and the Hilbert space dimension of 3D gravity
arxiv-2602-02645.creator: Vijay Balasubramanian, Rathindra Nath Das, Johanna Erdmenger, Jonathan Karl, Herman Verlinde
arxiv-2602-02645.description: Abstract A central problem in formulating a theory of quantum gravity is to determine the size and structure of the Hilbert space of black holes. Here we use a quantum dynamical Krylov complexity approach to calculate the Hilbert space dimension of a black hole in 2+1-dimensional Anti-de Sitter space.

pmc-11487386.title: Blackcurrant Pomace Extract as a Natural Antioxidant in Vienna Sausages Reformulated by Replacement of Pork Backfat with Emulsion Gels Based on High Oleic Sunflower and Flaxseed Oils
pmc-11487386.creator: Nicoleta Cîrstea (Lazăr), Violeta Nour, Alexandru Radu Corbu, Georgiana Gabriela Codină, Hongjie Dai
pmc-11487386.description: The incorporation of a blackcurrant pomace extract (BPE) at 2.5%, 5.0% and 10.0% into an emulsion gel based on high oleic sunflower and linseed oils was examined in order to obtain a functional ingredient to be used as a pork backfat replacer in Vienna sausages.

pmc-12664771.title: Causal Association Between Sleep Disorders and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Analysis for Clinical Practice
pmc-12664771.creator: Wenqiang Lu, Jianming Hu, Lihui Ding, Tao Feng, Le Li, Wentao Lei
pmc-12664771.description: Background: Sleep disorders have been associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary sisease (COPD) in observational studies, but causal inferences have not been confirmed. This bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study, combined with colocalization and enrichment analyses, aims to investigate the potential causal relationship between sleep-associated phenotypes and COPD.

pmc-13262435.title: Do carbon policy shocks move stocks? evidence from China’s carbon market
pmc-13262435.creator: Jiachao Peng, Yuxin Zeng, Shuke Fu, Jiali Tian
pmc-13262435.description: As carbon policies expand under net zero goals, policy news in carbon markets can send fast signals for equity prices. Using daily data for more than 1,600 listed firms from July 2021 to December 2025, we build carbon policy shocks from carbon price moves on 12 national ETS release days and estimate their link to stock returns.

pmc-13276838.title: Moving Beyond Fenton-Based Peroxidase Nanozymes for Analytical Sensing: Perspectives on Nonradical Alternatives from Heterogeneous Catalysis
pmc-13276838.creator: Bo Yuan, Yifan Cui, Pi-Tai Chou, Yung-Kang Peng
pmc-13276838.description: Artificial enzymes have garnered attention for their potential to overcome the cost and stability limitations of natural enzymes. Among these, nanozymessolid nanomaterials with enzymatic activityhave emerged as promising alternatives due to their facile synthesis and recyclability. To date, over half of the reported nanozymes mimic peroxidase (POD), catalyzing the oxidation of chromogenic substrates like 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) with H2O2.

pmc-13361190.title: Sintilimab-Induced Sequential Multi-System Severe Immune-Related Adverse Events in an Elderly Patient with Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13361190.creator: Xi Xia, Ting Yu, Hui Sun, Jian Li, Fengjun Liu, Xin Zhu
pmc-13361190.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can induce a spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), yet sequential, multi-organ severe irAEs remain uncommon and challenging to manage. We present a 78-year-old male patient with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, suspected to have developed continuous, life-threatening irAEs involving the liver, bone marrow, and lungs after receiving sintilimab combined with chemotherapy.

pmc-13407036.title: Integrating Pretreatment Circulating Tumor HPV DNA and Tumor Volume for Risk Stratification in HPV-Positive Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
pmc-13407036.creator: Lin Zhu, Chunying Shen, Wei Qian, Peiyao Liu, Tingting Xu, Huijuan Liu, Xin Zhou, Xueguan Lu
pmc-13407036.description: Simple SummarySome patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer still develop recurrence after treatment, and better tools are needed to identify high-risk patients early. This study evaluated circulating tumor HPV DNA in patients treated with induction therapy combined with definitive radiotherapy. Pretreatment circulating tumor HPV DNA was closely associated with tumor burden, especially lymph-node-related tumor volume.

pmc-13544672.title: Challenges in the initial diagnosis of colon carcinoma from symptoms of a bladder and colon fistula: a case report
pmc-13544672.creator: Jing-Hong Duan, Yu-Yun Wu, Wen-Bao Wang, Ye-Ping Zhang, Li-Ping Yang, Chao-Hua Deng
pmc-13544672.description: Introduction and importance:Sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma usually causes gastrointestinal complaints such as hematochezia or altered bowel habits. Urinary symptoms typically appear only in advanced disease. We describe an unusual case in which vesical fecaluria was the first and main symptom, mimicking recurrent urinary tract infection and risking delayed recognition of its colorectal origin.

pmc-13595151.title: Clinical course and biomarkers in patients with type 1 Gaucher disease and Parkinson's disease: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-13595151.creator: Ayuko Iverson, Drew B Sinha, Luca Fierro, Chanan Stauffer, Hetanshi Naik, Roy N Alcalay, Manisha Balwani
pmc-13595151.description: IntroductionPathogenic variants in GBA1, the gene encoding beta-glucocerebrosidase, are significant genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease (PD). Patients with type 1 Gaucher disease (GD1), caused by biallelic GBA1 variants, have approximately six-fold higher lifetime risk for PD compared to the general population. However, few studies have described the clinical presentation of GD-associated PD (GD-PD) in GD1 patients.
